interface: docs/scripts/reference-harness.mjs (recipes/<id>.json and journeys/<id>.json fragments resolved with manifest.json metadata into receipt.recipes and receipt.journeys; recipesGate and runJourneys options)

gate.enforcedWhen: the release lane turns the gate on when the first producing feature node (CSS0, WBC0, DBG0, TST0, RTI0, AX0, WPF0 or SEC0) supplies an executable recipe example with a capability link; until then every slot stays pending and the standard docs check runs without the gate
gate.rule: every topic must be supplied by a manifest example whose files include a file with an executable source extension (.ts/.mts/.cts/.js/.mjs/.cjs), whose entry is a shipped-bin command or a public import, and which cites at least one capability surface from the existing catalog; a static sample without an executable extension, an example without a capability link, a pending topic, or an unbound slot fails the gate

journeys.model: each journeys/<id>.json fragment is an ordered step program over registered example fragments; a step runs either an executable example file (NodeOnly) or a shipped-bin command declared by its example (NativeOnly), with declared args and expected exit codes
journeys.receiptBasis: executed journeys record per-step exit codes and stdout digests with engine and host identity under the WDX0 runtime-observation class; journeys that are not run are recorded not-run, never presented as executed

uncertaintyNotes: The recipe model requires real feature examples when the producing nodes land; today all eight slots are pending and no recipe page claims a working example. The journey executor is proven by real NodeOnly execution over the committed fixture home in tests/documentation/DOC5/fixtures; the declared cli-version-smoke journey needs the platform binary and is executed only on artifact-present lanes via --run-journeys, never faked as passed elsewhere.
permissions: the harness reads the repository and spawns the existing typeinfo freshness command; --run-journeys additionally spawns node child processes for journey steps (example files or shipped bin launchers) with a bounded per-step runtime, and installs no packages, writes no files and opens no network
migrationNotes: The reference harness resolves manifest.json metadata with <id>/example.json example fragments, recipes/<id>.json recipe topics and journeys/<id>.json journeys. Producing nodes update supplied status, example ids and capability surfaces in their own recipe fragment, register example fragments, and turn on --recipes-gate in the release lane. SDK guides use sdk-guides/<id>.json and --sdk-gate. Row arrays in the metadata header are rejected.
resourceRationale: synchronous static validation over a small authored tree; journey execution is opt-in, sequential and bounded at 60000 ms per step, so no unbounded latency, allocation or RSS budget is introduced and no ratified performance methodology measurement is claimed
